decisions.executionNote: Raise and turn right gripper toward a top-down basket approach; left arm stays parked. Small initial increments preserve elbow-up continuity.
Advance above the rear basket egg while completing most of the downward wrist rotation; remain clear of the rim.
Use the nearer, well-exposed egg instead. Finish vertical alignment and descend slowly with the gripper open.
Correct the wrist-to-finger offset toward the near egg, close fully, then make a small test lift to check retention visually.
Lift the near egg clear of the basket, keeping the grip closed. Begin a modest inward tilt for reaching the holder without crossing the arms.
Carry the visibly retained egg above the holder at clearance height, keeping the right elbow configuration continuous and the gripper closed.
Lower the retained egg toward the rear-right holder cup, with a slight forward correction. Keep closed until it is near the cup bottom.
An egg is visible in the rear-left cup and the wrist is close to the upright lid. Open and withdraw upward/backward before returning toward the basket.
Return above the basket's right-hand egg, reopening fully and restoring the near-vertical picking orientation.
Descend carefully over the right basket egg with fingers open, making a small centering correction before grasping.
Center fingers around the second egg, close fully, and test retention with a short vertical lift.
Lift the second egg clear of the basket before translating inward; hold fully closed and gently incline toward the holder.
Carry the second egg over the empty rear-right cup and start a slow approach, maintaining clearance from the upright lid.
The second egg is visibly free over the holder; open and clear the lid, then approach the remaining rear basket egg. Recheck seating from the next view.
Approach the rear basket egg slowly with fingers open. The second holder egg may be on a divider, so seating will need another visual check.
Advance a little toward the rear egg, lower to its sides, close, and make a short test lift. Verify the grasp from the wrist view.
Lift vertically with the gripper closed to test the rear-egg grasp, moving slightly away from the basket rim once clear.
The rear egg stayed in the basket. Reopen, recenter slightly toward the robot, and approach deeper so the fingers reach its sides rather than its top.
Close around the centered rear egg at the deeper approach, pause for contact, and lift gently to verify retention.
The rear egg is now retained. Lift clear and move toward the holder's front row, away from the upright lid, maintaining a closed grip.
Carry the third egg over the empty front-right cup, then descend partway while watching clearance from the two eggs already on the holder.
Lower the third egg into the front-right cup with a small centering correction, then open once near the holder bottom.
Withdraw vertically from the released third egg, then move toward the final basket egg. Reinspect the holder after clearing the view; some eggs may need centering.
Three eggs are now on the holder, including a seated front-right egg. Approach the remaining basket egg with an open, near-vertical gripper.
Center on the final basket egg and lower to its sides before closing. Make a short test lift, keeping the command fully closed.
The final egg slipped toward the basket's near side. Reopen and recenter over its new position before another careful grasp.
Shift the open gripper slightly left and nearer over the displaced egg, then close and test with a small lift.
The last egg appears retained between the fingers. Lift clear, keep fully closed, and begin moving toward the empty rear-right holder cup.
Carry the final egg to a clear position above the empty rear-right cup; maintain grip and pause above the other eggs before the final descent.
Lower the retained last egg toward the rear-right cup with a small forward and left correction, remaining closed until its seating depth is verified.
The last egg is aligned over the rear-right cup, but the wrist is contacting the lid. Release without pushing farther and withdraw upward/backward to inspect all four eggs.
All four eggs are visibly seated. Close the empty gripper and move above the lid's upper-right edge, preparing to fold it toward the holder.
Replan from the continuity stop using smaller forward increments, approaching just above the lid edge without pushing on the eggs.
Avoid the upper reach limit by lowering toward the lid edge, then gently draw the closed fingertips toward the holder to initiate closure.
The lid has begun rotating toward closed. Follow its arc gently toward the robot and downward, keeping the empty fingers together.
The lid is visibly closed. Open the empty gripper, retreat clear of the holder, and begin restoring the right arm to its starting pose.
Continue returning the right arm toward origin with a gradual wrist rotation and descent; correct the parked left arm's small drift.
Finish restoring both arms to their starting poses with tapering increments. The basket is empty and the holder lid remains visibly shut.
Make the final submillimeter origin correction and hold both arms still with open grippers, allowing the closed holder and robot to settle.
